rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and organization of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize comments clearly and logically: brief overview of main strengths and weaknesses, section-structured critique, prioritized concerns, and clear separation of major vs minor issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number comments, divide into major and minor criticisms, and prioritize concerns to help authors and editors. A well-organized review facilitates systematic author rebuttals and editorial evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include explicit examination of institutional incentives for IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating the research environment of institutions, include an explicit and detailed examination of the incentives for building IDR, including support for interdisciplinary communities, centres, and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward institutional policies and structures that foster healthy IDR ecosystems and career pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject reliance on authority; ground knowledge in facts and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject every kind of fiction and imposture and trust the evidence of facts rather than deriving authority from ancients or genealogies of prestige.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base conclusions on collected observations and experiments instead of appealing to earlier authorities. Anti-pattern: retrofitting new facts to conform to received systems or seeking legitimacy by tracing ideas to illustrious predecessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property, permissions, and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manuscript should contain only the authors' original work; all authors must certify the manuscript is a unique submission not under consideration elsewhere and not previously published in part or full (short abstracts at meetings are usually acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must secure written release prior to submission for any copyrighted excerpts, figures, tables, or audio/video files and obtain written releases from patients for names/likenesses; provide copies on request and be responsible for permission fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for specific study designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to consult and follow reporting guidelines relevant to their specific research design (e.g., CONSORT for randomized controlled trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CONSORT statement provides items to report and a patient flow diagram. Reporting guidelines exist for various study designs and some are available at www.consort-statement.org. Authors should consult the target journal's information for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting methods, decisions and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: All inclusion decisions, handling of overlap, search strategies, screening, extraction, quality assessments, and any post-hoc modifications must be documented with rationale in the protocol and final report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is required so readers can assess potential biases introduced by overview-level decisions (e.g. exclusion of poorly conducted SRs based on quality assessments). Provide supplementary materials (search strategies, characteristics of included/excluded reviews, data package). See V.4, V.5 and Boxes V.5.a/b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise observational data reporting (meteors, phenomena)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational reports should include precise times, positions (RA/Dec or bearing), magnitudes, counts, velocities, and lengths of visible course (example: positions of Draconic radiant across years, meteor observed at specific time and coordinates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear tabulation of positional data, times, brightness estimates, and any derived quantities to facilitate later comparison and analysis by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inductive conclusions go beyond their premises (generalisation requires evidential warrant)
rubrics_metrics.description: A principle ascertained by experience is more than a mere summing up of what was specifically observed; it is a generalisation grounded on cases and expressive of belief that what was found true is true in an indefinite number of unobserved cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appraising inductive arguments, demand appropriate evidential basis and consider whether the sample/cases justify generalising beyond observed instances; recognise induction adds substantive content needing support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical demonstration and reproducible experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about principles or substances should be supported by experiments that others can reproduce and examine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author stresses the need for experiments and offers examples (distillation mixtures, distilling olive oil with sal circulatum, the author's own retort experiments producing brimstone) while cautioning against relying solely on unverified reports (Helmont). Anti-pattern: asserting facts based only on cant or authority without experimental detail or reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and management of conflicts of interest affecting reviewers, authors, or editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 covers conflicts of interest so editors can recognise, declare, and mitigate COIs in review and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify composition, state, and handling conditions for reactive mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of fulminating gold and burning mixtures notes the importance of dryness/imbibition and whether precipitates have been dried or imbibed (e.g., 'if the precipitate should be dried, and imbibed sometimes with a spirit of urine, it will then recover its fulminating power').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting reactive or explosive combinations, list exact components, their proportions, physical state (dry/wet), and any preparatory or storage conditions that affect behavior (drying, impregnation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess scientific merit, originality, and scope; recommend improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining scientific merit, originality, and scope of the work; indicating ways to improve it; and, if requested, recommending acceptance or rejection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should identify strengths and weaknesses and provide concrete suggestions for improvement. In cases of controversy an additional review or editor evaluation may be solicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting reviewers is a crucial part of an editor’s work. We aim to engage researchers who are not only experts on the topic but who are also constructive, fair and timely in their assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors choose referees for both expertise and for the quality/constructiveness of their expected assessment; reviewer timeliness is an explicit consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and References
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy, relevance, completeness, and ethical use of citations and references supporting manuscript claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that every claim is supported by appropriate, verifiable references; assess currency and relevance of cited literature (include recent advances as well as foundational works); verify completeness — look for missing seminal works or important related studies; ensure consistent citation style and adequate bibliographic details for locating sources; encourage primary sources over secondary reviews when possible; evaluate contextualization of cited works and whether claims accurately reflect sources; watch for excessive self-citation and balance of external references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with journal-specific features and requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must adhere to the journal’s instructions to authors regarding writing, graphics, and formatting conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check items such as definition of abbreviations at first mention, legible fonts in tables/figures, referenced style requirements, and flag noncompliance to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks: usage and punctuation placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation marks: not to be used in connection with reduced citations, 87; exception to this rule, 75; placing of colon in connection with, 136; of comma, 162; of ellipsis, 181; of exclamation point, 128; of interrogation point, 130; of period, 126; rules for use of, 74-91; to be omitted in references to Preface, Index, etc., 82; use of double and single, 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when to use or omit quotation marks (titles, reduced citations), and how other punctuation relates to quotation marks; includes single vs double quotation preferences and exceptions (see §§74–91, 136, 162, 181).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections that fail to resolve issues (correction → retraction pathway)
rubrics_metrics.description: A published correction may later be followed by a full retraction if readers raise additional questions about the corrected material (example: a paper corrected in 2016 was later retracted when further concerns arose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections do not always settle concerns; persistent or new questions after a correction can escalate to retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing & Editorial Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: General policies on editorial processes, publication decisions, and related operational issues for journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad heading on index; full guidance addresses processes such as handling submissions, corrections, and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skin cleanliness (frequent ablution) as epidemic prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim: regular head-to-foot ablutions with tepid water reduced death-rate and sickness by one-third in children's institutions; trained nurses give whole-person ablutions twice a day and a change of clothes once a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate immediate and general 'tubbing' of population as a defensive regulation against epidemics, applied as sedulously as vaccination; note observed improvements in strength and assimilation among those bathed regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and report experimental geometry and distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify distances, orientations and relative motions (e.g., fork positions, distance 30–60 ft, moving-case movement) so effects can be interpreted and repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments reported include precise actions (e.g., holding fork 2 in hand 30–60 ft away; walking toward/away while screwing fork on/off its case; placing the fork on the case while in motion). Report whether the moving fork was placed on or removed from its case, the time of stopping/starting, and the ear/eye observation points (assistant’s ear close to case while eye on screen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timeliness and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Please strive to complete your review within 3 weeks of accepting a review request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will aim to remind reviewers of upcoming and past due dates. Editors may assign additional or alternate reviewers if a review is excessively late. Contact the editor directly or in the submission thread to inform them about possible delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials — machine-readable and repository guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged or required to provide all datasets on which conclusions rely, either by depositing in publicly available repositories or presenting them in the main paper/additional files; provide datasets in a machine-readable format (e.g., spreadsheets rather than PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not link to data on personal/departmental websites. For databases include web/ftp address and usage restrictions. For software include: project name, project home page, archived version DOI, operating system(s), programming language, other requirements, license, and any restrictions to use by non-academics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper–reviewer assignment methodology and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Affinities for matching included the expertise model, reviewer bids, and conflicts of interest. Optimization used Min-Cost-Flow and FairFlow; optimizer meta-parameters are tunable and chairs ran the optimizer many times (~60 minute turnaround). Each match comes with summary statistics about match quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-factor affinity scoring (expertise, bids, COIs) and advanced optimizers; provide tunable hyperparameters, quick re-run ability, and match-quality diagnostics. Allow browsing/editing of assignment results via UI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract terms possess single intension and are incapable of plurality
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract terms are strongly distinguished from general terms by possessing only one kind of meaning; for they denote qualities there is nothing which they cannot inhere in of red objects, but this latter term has one single meaning — the quality alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'redness' denotes the single quality shared by red objects and so is one and the same everywhere. Speaking of 'rednesses' introduces concreteness (different kinds or tints) and so alters meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of the Composition of Causes (general rule of causation)
rubrics_metrics.description: More of the cause is followed by more of the effect (composition of causes), except in special cases where causes change properties when conjoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as a general heuristic for causal expectation (used to motivate concomitant variation thinking), but remain alert to exceptional cases where causes interact and change properties when combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evidence among related species (inference from variation in allied taxa)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sexes of the several species differ much in length, irrespective of that of the male; and this can be accounted for... by the laws of inheritance—that is by the successive variations having been from the first more or less closely limited in their transmission to the male sex—than by the agency of natural selection, resulting from the length of tail being more or less injurious to the females of these several allied species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare patterns across closely related species (e.g., tail lengths among pheasants) to assess whether differences are better explained by inheritance laws or by direct natural-selection pressures on females. Consistent interspecific patterns favor inheritance explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers should keep their own identities anonymous (referee anonymity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal does not release reviewers' identities to authors or other reviewers unless reviewers request identification. Reviewers should not identify themselves to authors without the Editorial Office's knowledge; if they wish to reveal their identities, do so via the publishing office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review (transparency of review records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-review decisions and author responses for published papers are available for all to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife makes review histories public for published papers to increase transparency and allow readers to see decision context, reviewer concerns, and author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustiveness: every idea is from sensation or reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: The understanding seems to me not to have the least glimmering of any ideas which it doth not receive from one of these two. EXTERNAL OBJECTS furnish the mind with the ideas of sensible qualities... and THE MIND furnishes the understanding with ideas of its own operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological test: when investigating any supposed idea, try to trace it back to either sensation or reflection. This is used to reject claims of other origins (notably innate ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals: spelling, figures, punctuation, and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to spell out numbers versus set in figures, treatment of consecutive numbers, groups, round numbers, use of commas for thousands, use of dash for ranges, and spacing of numerals in lines/headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers commencing a sentence to be spelled out (96); connected groups to be treated alike (94); groups of six or more closely connected to be set in figures (94); numbers of less than three digits spelled out in ordinary reading matter (94); round numbers treatment (95); use of comma after digits indicating thousands (159); use of comma to separate numbers (154); dash as 'to' connecting numbers (173); Arabic and Roman numerals spacing at beginning of lines and headlines (271); omission of period after numerals (124).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dividing compounds, prefixes, and suffixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenated or closed compounds and words with prefixes/suffixes are best divided at natural morphological breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'poverty‑/stricken (not pov‑/erty‑stricken)'; 'dis‑pleasure (rather than displea‑sure)'; 're‑inforce (not rein‑force)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review evaluates the quality of a manuscript before publication by independent researchers in the field; typically two or more experts evaluate manuscripts based on scientific robustness, originality, and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' feedback guides editors' decisions; editors may consult editorial board members. BMC Neurology operates transparent peer review: if published, reviewer reports are published online under a Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 but reviewers are not named. Reviewers and editors must declare competing interests and can be excluded if a competing interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of human nature must connect generalizations to underlying laws
rubrics_metrics.description: To have genuine scientific character, approximate generalizations must be connected deductively with the laws of nature from which they result, showing their proper limits and enabling deduction in new circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The value of social generalizations increases when they can be exhibited as corollaries of universal laws, permitting extension and delimitation beyond mere empirical regularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of titles and forms of address
rubrics_metrics.description: When academic, civil, military, nobility, honorary, and other titles are capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic titles abbreviated (22); civil and military titles capitalization rules (21); 'President' and certain University of Chicago officers capitalization specifics (21, 49); titles not capitalized when spelled out in some contexts (22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide morphological description and measurements in natural-history observations
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting specimens (worms, anatomical features), give detailed morphology, counts, measurements, positions, and comparisons with known descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worms are described by length, thickness, colour, ring structure, position in gut, and compared to other authors and genera; such details enable identification and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support assertions with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantiate critiques with data, calculations, references, links, or other concrete evidence rather than unsupported claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to primary sources, underlying datasets, code, re-analyses, or independent replication attempts where available. Explain the method you used to check or reanalyze results. Evidence-based comments are more useful and more likely to remain on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and research ethics — duty to report concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers should take responsibility for reporting concerns regarding unethical practice (fabricated data, falsified data, stealing data, animal welfare breaches, duplicate/multiple submission and publication, unjustified or ghost authorship, conflicts of interest). Notify the editorial office if you suspect a breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most journals have procedures to investigate concerns without revealing your identity; give examples of misconduct (definitions provided) and let the editorial office handle investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical treatise: define images and judge appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘he propounds some theorems, from which the chief symptoms of refracted rays do result, their interjections and limits are easily discernible; the appearing places or images of such points are defined, both in regard to an eye situated in the axis of the radiation, and in regard to one placed elsewhere.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include theorems leading to observable symptoms of refracted rays; determine limits and intersections; define apparent places/images for different eye positions; provide determinations of places in the axis of the images for each kind of lens; give worked examples so the material is ‘ready, and serviceable to practise.’ Also treat accompanying phenomena (nature of light, colours, rainbows, prisms) and show how plain objects yield images and how they may be delineated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine multiple statistical metrics for comprehensive assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies combined kappa, ICC, percent agreement, sensitivity/specificity, and Cronbach's alpha to present a multifaceted view of reliability and validity (examples across multiple abstracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a suite of complementary statistics tailored to outcome type (categorical vs continuous vs diagnostic) to provide a robust picture of measurement performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility for teachers and school officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is valuable because it is 'practical' and 'the author devotes the last hundred pages to laying down courses of study, general and special' — a constructive portion for organizing instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuals should provide actionable course plans and practical systems that have stood the test of experience; constructive, implementable guidance is especially prized even if tentative.
